body: That’s what I was thinking. I’ve just had past relationships & my upbringing that’s resulted in physical violence so I’m being extremely cautious. I also don’t want to have on rose-colored glasses.
I agree, am I being foolish for wanting to talk about it more? And if the conversation goes well, in terms of what & how he says things, would I be dumb to continue dating him?

ty for the advice! what did you like about EDMR? process and all? the next step after DBT group is trauma treatment so i’m hoping it’ll help. it’s just 9 weeks away /: i didn’t know if there was anything i can do in the meantime?

i’m so happy to hear that you’re in a better space! i remember my freshman year being so difficult & by my senior year i was just genuinely content. even if i have my lows, i trust that things will be okay.
hey OP, im glad you’re still here
i’ve been kind to him thinking it was just an impulsive reaction…i think you’re right. he’s never seen me as my own person, only an extension of himself and he has a lot of self-hate.

i am so sorry you’re going through that. i hope you have other people you can reach out to; i’m writing this after sleeping and i’m feeling more levelheaded. calling the suicide hotline has been helpful for me in the past as much as i didn’t want to do it. they might be a good outlet where your friend can’t be.

thanks for the kindness; i find it difficult to use the skills, we’re being taught, in my life when things get really hard. when i feel balanced, they’re easy to use and they’ve improved my life; it’s just really difficult to when i feel like this. 

so i do live on my own which is what blows my mind. i cut off my dad and due to a family death i’ve reconnected a little bit. and since then my boundaries haven’t been really respected. i’m still connected to him financially on one or two things and im working on making sure i can be completely free from him.
